maria (eng-runtime): Heads up — noticed a sharp throughput drop in prod-eu-1 starting ~12:11 UTC. Multiple workers in pool-gamma restarted and several GPUs logged OOMs. Seeing kernel selector flip a few times. Can SRE triage?
kevin (eng-ml): I pulled metrics — p95 latency for model-text-open-1 spiked from ~75ms to ~420ms, throughput -30%. Kernel fallback to `generic-attn` correlated with the spike.
ashwin typo? No: ashwin (eng-sre): On it. Initial logs show repeated worker restarts (exit code 137) and allocator churn. `dmesg` has container oom kills around the same window.
jules (eng-runtime): Reproduced on staging: adaptive batching allowed batches to grow during a short request surge. Combined with a KV cache insert burst, we end up needing a large contiguous temp buffer during the new kernel path which fails. Kernel selector then falls back to a slower implementation.
maria (eng-runtime): Snippet from worker log: ```alloc_impl.cpp:278 allocate failed size=0x1000000 pid=1234``` multiple nodes show `worker exited with code 137`.
ashwin (eng-sre): nvml shows ~2GB free on some GPUs but allocator reports 'no contiguous block' failures — classic fragmentation. Also seeing high KV eviction rates in the same window.
perf-bot: [perf-regression] model-text-open-1: p99 +320% coincident with commit `a3f2d` (batching heuristic tweak) on 2026-03-12.
kevin (eng-ml): Temporary mitigation: cap auto-grow max_batch to 64 for pool-gamma and consider pinning kernel list to the stable profile to avoid fallback.
jules (eng-runtime): Did a quick mitigation: disabled `adaptive_batching.enabled` on pool-gamma and drained the biggest noisy tenant (tenant-47) to a separate pool. After that throughput recovered ~18% and OOMs stopped.
maria (eng-runtime): Nice. Still need a root cause: hypothesis is allocator fragmentation driven by large KV cache insert bursts combined with temp buffers used by the new kernel path.
ashwin (eng-sre): Scheduling a profiling window at 15:00 UTC — will capture malloc traces, jemalloc stats, and nvprof snapshots. Can runtime add a metric for kernel fallback counts?
jules (eng-runtime): Yes — will add `kernel_selector.fallback_count` and `batch.size_histogram`. Also prototype a background KV compaction run to reduce fragmentation.
kevin (eng-ml): Suggest adding a guard in the batch heuristic: only auto-grow if contiguous_free_mem > threshold. That should avoid triggering large contiguous allocations during bursts.
maria (eng-runtime): Filing follow-up ticket INF-8421 with logs, mitigations, and action items. Thanks all :thumbsup:
ashwin (eng-sre): Keeping this as Sev2 until we validate compaction and metrics in canary. Alerting rule: `kernel_selector.fallback_count > 5/min` configured.
maria (eng-runtime): Once compaction + metrics are live, plan a canary rollout with gradual exposure and perf-eval to verify no regressions.
